title: panel-ops-standup-capture-2026-06-20
body:
Panel ops standup — 2026-06-20 (async capture)

Attendees: Maya (notes), Eliot, Samira, Connor, Jen (prod), + optional: ops-on-call
Duration: ~20m async + 10m follow-up live if needed

Purpose: quick health + blocking items across UI, rollout orchestration, and rollout analytics; keep a single action list for the next 48–72h.

AGENDA
- Quick health signal (live metrics / incidents)
- UI: blocking bugs, UX shims for rollout failures
- Rollouts: canary cadence, fallback incidents, policy updates
- Analytics: missing telemetry, drift alarms, dashboard gaps
- Actions and owners

QUICK HEALTH
- No Sev1s overnight. Latency SLOs: console API p95 trending 210ms (target 200) — small uptick observed between 02:00–04:00 PDT due to query fanout from rollout-simulator (investigating).
- One customer reported stale rollout state in UI (REDW-4212) — repro steps in Linear; appears UX state cache not invalidating when coordination service fails a partial write.

UI NOTES / BLOCKERS
- Stale rollout state (REDW-4212) — root cause: local memory cache invalidation missed on 409 conflict from orchestration service. Temporary mitigation: reduce cache TTL to 30s for rollout list view (Samira will ship hotspot patch).
- Canary progress bar shows 0% on successful canary completion in some edge cases — suspected race between websocket update and polling refresh. Connor to add debounce and force-refresh on socket reconnect.
- Accessibility issue in rollout details: keyboard focus trapped inside expanded variant card — low priority but assigned to Eliot (small DOM-order fix).
- UX shim proposal: introduce an explicit “refresh state” button visible to admins when there’s a mismatch between console and orchestration (MVP). Action: Maya to draft copy and mock, link to playbook.

ROLLOUT/ORCHESTRATION NOTES
- Canary cadence experiment: next week we test faster 5-minute canaries with increased sampling for low-risk model variants. Plan: run on internal-only endpoints first. Jen to coordinate and provide experiment tags for analytics.
- Fallback policy changes: add a soft-fallback state that preserves session continuity when a model variant is unavailable, instead of hard-failing generation. Decision: proceed, risk doc in confluence; Samira to create a feature flag and run behind kill-switch.
- Rollout simulator load: observed query-fanout causing console p95 bump overnight — follow-ups: (1) add per-simulator rate cap (Connor), (2) route simulator traffic to a dedicated read replica (platform infra).

ANALYTICS / OBSERVABILITY
- Missing telemetry: no reliable event emitted when rollout cache invalidation is skipped — need an event on conflict path. Action: Eliot to add a telemetry event and wire it to the rollout-health dashboard.
- Dashboard gaps: the "canary success by variant" tile is stale for last 24h (ingestion lag). Ops: check ingestion worker backpressure and partition offsets. Linked issue: REDW-4387.
- Drift alarms: suggestion to add a "UI state drift" anomaly detector that correlates server-side truth vs client-reported state (Jen). Agreed as spike next sprint (2d).

DECISIONS TAKEN
- Reduce rollout list cache TTL to 30s for immediate mitigation (temp change), monitor for extra read load.
- Implement soft-fallback behavior behind feature flag.
- Ship telemetry on cache-invalidation-conflict path before end of sprint.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- Does lowering TTL increase DB reads beyond commit threshold for Dedicated customers? Need cost estimate and opt-out path. (Maya)
- Can simulator traffic be throttled at LB level vs app level? Which is less invasive? (Connor)
- UX: is "refresh state" button confusing for self-serve customers? Consider only showing for admin role. (Eliot)

ACTIONS (owner — due)
- Samira: patch to reduce rollout list cache TTL to 30s; add feature flag to revert quickly — due 2026-06-21 — linked: https://linear.app/REDW-4212
- Connor: debounce socket reconnect path + force refresh on reconnect; add per-simulator rate cap PR — due 2026-06-22 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/998
- Eliot: add telemetry event for cache-invalidation-conflict and wire to rollout-health dashboard; create dashboard tile for "UI state drift" spike spec — due 2026-06-23
- Jen: coordinate canary cadence experiment and provide experiment tags + success criteria; post-run summary to #rollouts and link to confluence doc — due 2026-06-24
- Maya: draft mock and copy for "refresh state" admin button and attach to playbook — due 2026-06-22 — confluence: confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Panel+Rollout+Playbook

MINOR / NICE-TO-HAVE
- Accessibility sweep for variant card (Eliot)
- Add small tooltip explaining "soft-fallback" behavior in rollout docs (Samira)

FOLLOW-UP MEETING / CHECKPOINTS
- Quick sync Friday AM (15m) if any action fails or we see SLO degradation. Otherwise update thread in #console-tooling with status.

RAW NOTES / DISCUSSION FRAGMENTS
- "Simulator traffic spiked because QA left a stress job running overnight — we should have auto-tagging + TTL on internal sim runs." — Connor
- "If we ship TTL change, we should coordinate with Dedicated ops — don't want unexpected read costs." — Jen
- "I'm going to add a tiny telemetry event even if we don't fully fix the flow this sprint — helps root cause faster." — Eliot

ATTACHMENTS / LINKS (quick)
- Linear: REDW-4212 (stale rollout state), REDW-4387 (dashboard lag)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/998
- Playbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Panel+Rollout+Playbook
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C04ROLL/ppp-standup-2026-06-20

END (save & ping)

-- Maya
notes: rough capture; will convert to checklist and update linear tasks after patches land.
